AfterPlayerTurnStart.issue: Rollup of guards G1 and G2 per binding rule 4. The effect is right -- 5 distinct pool cards on turn 1, each given Retain, one chosen into hand -- but they are rolled on the wrong RNG stream with the wrong draw algorithm (G1), and the sim maps AfterPlayerTurnStart and AfterSideTurnStart onto one method, losing C#'s guarantee that this relic resolves before every AfterSideTurnStart listener (G2).

guards.what: G1 (LIVE for parity): the card generation uses the legacy shared RNG and `rng.sample`, where C# names CombatCardGeneration and does an UnstableShuffle-take-first
guards.issue: Closed 2026-07-27: the port now draws on the named stream. sts2_rl/relics/choices_paradox.py:32-38 branches on `crng.is_parity` into `get_distinct_for_combat_parity(crng.card_gen, 5)`, the UnstableShuffle-then-Take port over CombatCardGeneration that ChoicesParadox.cs:34 passes to CardFactory.GetDistinctForCombat; legacy keeps random_pool_cards on the shared Random. WAS: the call went to the legacy shared random.Random, so the stream was never advanced and every later draw off it read at the wrong position.

guards.what: G2 (DORMANT): AfterPlayerTurnStart (step 22) and AfterSideTurnStart (step 23) are two different C# hooks collapsed onto one sim method
guards.issue: PROMPT.md bug class 15 -- when the sim maps two C# hooks onto one method, list both call sites. C# fires Hook.AfterPlayerTurnStart at the end of SetupPlayerTurn, per player, immediately after that player's draw (CombatManager.cs:673-675 = audit/records/seam/turn_structure.json step 22), and Hook.AfterSideTurnStart only afterwards, once EVERY player's setup has finished (CombatManager.cs:520-524 = step 23). Both map to the sim's single on_player_turn_started (hooks.py:285-295), so ChoicesParadox's guaranteed position ahead of every AfterSideTurnStart listener becomes listener-registration order. Confirmed by execution that the sim really does have only one slot there (`py audit/tools/relic_probes.py turn-order` prints exactly one on_player_turn_started per turn). Same family as audit/records/seam/turn_structure.json guard G12, which flattens the VeryEarly/Early/Late SUB-phases of a single hook; this is the coarser version -- two distinct hooks, not two sub-phases -- so it is recorded here rather than folded in. DORMANT: the divergence needs an AfterSideTurnStart listener that reads the hand on turn 1, and the ported turn-1 AfterSideTurnStart content does not -- relic/candelabra and relic/chandelier gate on turns 2 and 3, and the turn-1 hand readers (relic/cloak_clasp) sit at turn END. Porting or writing any turn-1 AfterSideTurnStart effect that counts cards in hand makes it live.

guards.what: G3: the softlock guard -- `if (list.Count == 0) { Log.Error; SentryService.CaptureException; return; }` (ChoicesParadox.cs:35-41) vs `if not options: return` (choices_paradox.py:32-33)
guards.rationale: Same early return; the logging and Sentry legs are diagnostics with no model effect. Recorded because the guard exists precisely so an empty pool cannot hang a selection screen, and the sim's CombatState.select_cards would return [] rather than hang -- so the port is safe for the same reason twice over.

guards.what: G4: the card pool -- `Character.CardPool.GetUnlockedCards(UnlockState, RunState.CardMultiplayerConstraint)` then FilterForCombat (ChoicesParadox.cs:34) vs `pool_card_ids()` over IRONCLAD_POOL (cards/pool.py:100-117 via random_pool_cards)
guards.rationale: FilterForCombat is what pool_card_ids ports -- exclude Basic and Ancient rarities and anything with CanBeGeneratedInCombat false, in pool order -- and get_distinct_for_combat_parity's docstring states the equivalence. The UnlockState argument assumes full unlocks, which is the sim's global assumption (the same assumption .superpowers/sdd/content-relic-sweeps.md sweep B flags for relic/lasting_candy), and CardMultiplayerConstraint is single-player. Note the contrast with the REWARD pool, which uses the unfiltered GetUnlockedCards -- this is the combat-generation path, so the filter is correct here.

guards.what: G5: `CardCmd.ApplyKeyword(item, CardKeyword.Retain)` on all five options (ChoicesParadox.cs:42-45) vs `card.retain = True` (choices_paradox.py:34-35)
guards.rationale: cards/base.py:78 declares `retain: bool = False`, so the sim has the real keyword and the assignment sticks. Both sides apply Retain to every generated option and not only to the chosen one -- harmless, since the four unchosen cards are discarded without ever entering a pile on either side, but worth confirming it is not an off-by-one in the port.
